_note: Static text shown on step cards. The optional narrator may rephrase it but never changes facts. {model}, {sizeGb}, {context} are filled by core.

scan-pc.what: Checking what your PC can do.
scan-pc.why: So I pick an AI that runs well here, not one that freezes your PC.
scan-pc.requiredReason: I need this to choose the right AI for your PC.

choose-model.what: Choosing the best AI model that fits your PC: {model}.
choose-model.why: A model that is too big runs very slowly. Too small gives weaker answers.
choose-model.changes: Nothing yet. You can see why I chose it.
choose-model.requiredReason: An AI model is needed to answer you.

install-runtime.what: Installing Ollama, the free program that runs the AI.
install-runtime.why: The AI model needs a program to run it, like a music file needs a player.
install-runtime.changes: Adds one program (Ollama), about 1 GB of disk (estimate). You can remove it later.
install-runtime.requiredReason: Without Ollama the AI cannot run.
install-runtime.notNeeded: Ollama is already installed. I will use it as it is.

download-model.why: This is the AI itself. After this, it works without internet.
download-model.changes: Uses about {sizeGb} GB of disk (estimate). Removable later.
download-model.requiredReason: The AI model is what answers your questions.
download-model.notNeeded: This model is already on your PC.

safe-defaults.what: Setting safe settings for your PC's memory.
safe-defaults.why: So the AI remembers enough of the conversation ({context} tokens) without running out of memory.
safe-defaults.changes: Saves one Ollama setting. The old value is kept so it can be restored.
safe-defaults.requiredReason: Wrong settings can make the AI slow or crash.

speed-boost.what: Optional speed boost: a small helper AI guesses ahead, and your main AI checks its guesses.
speed-boost.why: Answers can come faster. It needs spare graphics memory, and your graphics card has some left over.
speed-boost.changes: Adds one program, llama.cpp (about 1 GB, estimate). Advanced and optional.
speed-boost.notNeeded: Your PC doesn't need this. It only helps on a PC with a separate graphics card.
speed-boost.notNeededFull: Not offered: your graphics card's memory is already used by the AI model, so there is no spare room for the helper.
speed-boost.disabled: Your PC could use the speed boost, but it isn't ready in this version. I haven't finished testing it, so I'm leaving it out. Your AI works without it, just without the extra speed. There's nothing to do here.

remote-access.what: Installing Tailscale so your other devices can reach this AI.
remote-access.why: It creates a private network between only your own devices. Nothing is opened to the internet.
remote-access.changes: Adds one program (Tailscale). You will sign in to your own free account. Removable later.
remote-access.signInNote: A Tailscale window will open. Sign in with your own account. I never see your password.
remote-access.refused: I won't set this up: something on this PC already uses Tailscale sharing, and changing it could break it.
remote-access.disabled: Using your AI from your other devices isn't available yet in this version. I haven't finished testing it, so I'm leaving it out. For now, your AI works on this PC only. There's nothing to do here.

connect-coding-tool.what: Connecting your coding tool to this AI.
connect-coding-tool.why: So your coding tool uses your private AI instead of a paid online one.
connect-coding-tool.changes: Writes one settings file for the coding tool. Any old file is backed up first.

workflow-rules.what: Offering a ready-made rules file for coding projects (optional).
workflow-rules.why: It reminds the AI to plan, build, then check its work. Helpful, not required.
workflow-rules.changes: Saves one text file only if you choose a folder for it.

test-run.what: Sending a real test question to your new AI.
test-run.why: To prove it works and measure its real speed on your PC.
test-run.changes: Nothing. Just one question and answer.

claudeCodeHeader: # Use your local AI in Claude Code, in this PowerShell window only.
# Closing this window puts Claude Code back to normal. Nothing on this PC is changed.
rulesFile: # How the AI should work in this project
<!-- Added by SetupPilot. Optional: edit it to suit you, or delete it. -->
These are suggestions, not requirements. Change anything you like.
- Before changing code, write a short plan: what will change, in which files, and why.
- If the task is unclear, ask one question instead of guessing.
- Wait for my OK on the plan before starting.
- Change one thing at a time, small enough to review.
- Ask before deleting files or running commands that change this computer.
- After each change, run the project's tests, or say how to check it by hand.
- Show what you ran and what happened. If something failed, say so plainly.
- Don't say something works until it has been checked.
- Claude Code reads this file because it is named CLAUDE.md. Other tools may ignore it.
- A small local AI can miss instructions. Keep tasks short and check its answers.
